note: Florida governor and U.S. Senate races, researched Oct. 25, 2026.

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
candidates.bio: U.S. representative for Florida's 19th District since 2021 and a former state representative.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds stands with the pro-life movement, opposes writing Roe v. Wade into law and voted against the Women's Health Protection Act (H.R. 3755, 2021)
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds says states should regulate abortion
source.quote: Regulating abortion is the job of the states.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted against the 2022 clean energy investments, to repeal them in 2023 and to end the tax credits in 2025
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds sponsored H.R. 4300 to bar presidents from declaring a climate emergency and said heat waves aren't tied to climate change

guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted to ease environmental rules for chip plants (S. 2228) and to end mining limits near the Boundary Waters (2026), though he backs fighting algal blooms
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted for the federal private school scholarship tax credit (2025) and says education dollars should follow students
source.quote: School choice is the civil rights issue of our time.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted against extending ACA premium subsidies for three years (House roll call 11, 2026) and opposes the ACA
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds would cut construction permit costs
source.quote: On housing, we are going to slash red tape.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted for the 2023 border wall bill (H.R. 2) and introduced a bill to study a biometric entry-exit system
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted for $75 billion more for ICE and $70 billion more for DHS and opposes sanctuary policies
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted for H.R. 2 (2023), which requires E-Verify for new hires
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted against the PRO Act (2021) and the 2026 first-contract bill (H.R. 5408) and supports right-to-work laws
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted to make providing gender-affirming care to minors a federal crime (H.R. 3492)
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds voted to bar transgender students from girls' sports (H.R. 734, 2023)
source.quote: Men SHOULD NOT be competing in women's sports PERIOD.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds opposed 2024's Amendment 3 and would oppose future legalization measures
source.quote: I do not support recreational marijuana.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds would cut taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds opposes raising taxes and voted to extend the 2017 tax cuts (2025)
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds supports 2026's Amendment 3, phasing out property taxes on many owner-occupied homes
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds supports voter ID and sponsored H.R. 7300, requiring proof of citizenship to register
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Donalds sponsored H.R. 7300, which bans universal vote-by-mail

candidates.name: David Jolly
candidates.bio: Republican U.S. representative for Florida's 13th District from 2014 to 2017, now running as a Democrat.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would replace Florida's six-week ban with a law allowing abortion until fetal viability
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would repeal Florida's six-week abortion ban
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would expand clean and renewable energy and build it into public utilities
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly on climate
source.quote: faces some of the most direct climate impacts in the country

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly calls for a data center moratorium until Florida has real protections for water and air
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly opposes offshore drilling
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports Everglades restoration and septic-to-sewer conversions to protect springs
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports a state version of the federal FIRST STEP Act to reduce recidivism
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would keep Florida's voucher program but reform it
source.quote: We should keep choice, but improve the standards of our choice schools.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports expanding Medicaid
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports extending the ACA premium tax credits
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly proposes a pilot program to expand community health centers with a 9-to-1 federal match
source.quote: 5-year pilot to dramatically expand community health centers

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports down-payment assistance
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports a path to legal status for long-term residents, parents of U.S. citizens and DACA recipients
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would not require state or local police to work with ICE
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly opposes mandating E-Verify
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would stand with public servants on fair wages and benefits
source.quote: proud to have the support of the Florida AFL-CIO.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly would protect marriage equality at the state level
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly calls attacks on LGBTQ+ people shameful but doesn't think biological males should play competitive women's sports
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly voted against 2024's Amendment 3 but would enact any amendment that won a majority, including recreational marijuana
guides.vote, 2026 Florida governor voters guide: Jolly supports home rule and easier citizen ballot initiatives
source.quote: Direct democracy should be easier, not a gauntlet.

candidates.name: Ashley Moody
candidates.bio: U.S. senator since January 2025, appointed to succeed Marco Rubio, and Florida attorney general from 2019 to 2025.

source.title: OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody cosponsored the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and a bill raising penalties for medical professionals who mishandle abortions (Florida Politics, Oct. 2025)
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: As attorney general, Moody fought to keep the abortion-rights amendment off Florida's ballot
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody has long backed school choice (FOX 13, Aug. 2025)
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody hailed the 2025 tax and spending law's tax cuts (Florida Phoenix, July 2025)
Florida Phoenix, Sept. 9, 2026: Moody was among the Republicans in Congress who let the enhanced ACA subsidies expire
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: As attorney general, Moody opposed the 2024 recreational marijuana ballot measure
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody supports enhanced penalties under the Thin Blue Line Act (2025)
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: As attorney general, Moody sued the federal government over carbon dioxide limits
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody supports the administration's immigration enforcement policies (2025)
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody says Florida stands with its ally Israel
OnTheIssues, 2026 Florida Senate race: Moody says government wastes hundreds of millions a year and backed the Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act (2025)

source.title: FOX 13 interview, July 8, 2026: Nixon supports a step-by-step path to Medicare for All
FOX 13 interview, July 8, 2026: Nixon would start by extending the ACA subsidies

Florida Phoenix, Sept. 9, 2026: Nixon calls for raising the federal minimum wage from $7.25 an hour

FOX 13 interview, July 8, 2026: Nixon would add funding for down payment assistance

FOX 13 interview, July 8, 2026: Nixon wants billionaires and corporations to pay their fair share
